content:
I'm about to submit a bunch of number theory roadmaps as PRs (@Chris Birkbeck has already started reviewing them on my fork), and I had a question about how roadmaps can depend on each other (since mine currently do). Here are some possible policies (I'm skipping mathlib since everything is allowed to depend on mathlib):

  1. Each layer in a roadmap PR may only depend on previous layers within that roadmap and finished layers within Tau Ceti.
  2. Each layer in a roadmap PR may only depend on previous layers within that roadmap and merged roadmaps (not necessarily implemented).
  3. Each layer in a roadmap PR may only depend on previous layers within that roadmap and explicitly named other roadmap PRs. PRs may only be merged when the roadmaps they depend on are completely implemented.
  4. Each layer in a roadmap PR may only depend on previous layers within that roadmap and explicitly named other roadmap PRs. PRs may only be merged when the layers within other roadmaps they depend on are completely implemented.
  5. Each layer in a roadmap PR may only depend on previous layers within that roadmap and explicitly named other roadmap PRs. PRs may only be merged when the roadmaps they depend on have been merged.

Does Tau Ceti have a policy along these lines? I think 3-5 may be technically annoying since stacking PRs on Github is only possible when all the branches are in the same repository (not in different forks), and thus later PRs will show all of the changes for PRs that they depend on.
Maybe as simple as roadmap can depend on merged roadmaps, impls can depend on merged impls (besides the layer-wise dependencies)?

I tried stack draft PRs for lean code but the current process is not designed for it yet. I switched to stack locally, and monitor will wake agent to submit new PR when prerequisite PR stablized (e.g. ready to merge).

Reading the wall of text I assume you want 5, so you can submit later PRs by just naming but not including needed roadmap PRs. That should work as long as they don't stack as PRs?

The benefit of 5 is that reviewers can review PRs simultaneously even while dependencies are under review. I just submitted 5 roadmaps for review (#188 through #192), but I have 14 more waiting. So being able to get these reviewed simultaneously would be really nice. But I think it's somewhat dangerous to not have the dependency included. I guess one modification of 3-5 would be to require that they be opened as draft PRs....
I don't think the issues you observed with stacked PRs to TauCeti itself are necessarily issues for TauCetiRoadmap, but there may be other problems.

Yeah, the issues don't apply directly, but the solution might. It might help if most PRs stay draft, agents can prioritize (e.g. based on the lean side work blocked by them) to keep a few ready for human attention bandwidth. (I can't even fully keep up with my own agents, and have to pace them sometimes.)

B.T.W. I might work on roed-math/TauCetiRoadmap#4 and roed-math/TauCetiRoadmap#7 (on the lean side) after SpinRepresentations.

(I should also say that I am genuniely excited to see so much basic number theory being proposed for Tau Ceti)
